chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Muhrim (one in Ihram) who hunts game, he said (peace be upon him): The expiation is upon him for every thing he catches.

key_terms.المُحْرِم: One in the state of Ihram, a ritual status for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a Muhrim who hunts game?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies that the expiation (kaffarah) for hunting while in Ihram is incurred per individual catch rather than as a single lump sum, a nuance critical for juristic calculations. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise liability in ritual purity laws, ensuring that repeated hunting acts trigger distinct compensations for each instance.
